label: paragraph_title
text: PEACE MOVES.

label: text
text: ASSURING NEWS FROM CANTON.

label: text
text:
From the tone of a letter received yesterday by Mr. Wong Tong, it appears that some of the "points" raised at Tuesday night's conference in Canton will be modified.
Mr. Wong of the On Lok Yuen Co., was mainly responsible for sending the Chinese delegates from Hongkong to negotiate, with Canton, an end to the strike.
The letter to Mr. Wong stated that the military, civil and labour authorities of Canton were very friendly to the Hongkong representatives. Certain demands at first raised would be changed for submission to a second conference which was to have sat last night.
Mr. Wong, attributed the delay in news getting through to the temporary dislocation of the cable services. He was confident that excellent results would be forthcoming. His opinion was based on the warm welcome extended to the delegates, and the elaborate precautions regarding a private train with poured cars for prevention conveying troops. Mr. Wong felt that a much better tone would have prevailed at last night.

label: text
text: The Legislative Council this afternoon considered for fully five minutes this afternoon the definition "floating fish" in a provision of an Ordinance relating to stealing oysters from oyster bed laying or fisheries.

text: The object of the proviso was stated by the Hbn. Attorney-General to be for the purpose of allowing net or other fishing which did not interfere with oyster beds.

label: text
text: THE REPORT NOT YET READY.

label: text
text: The collection by examination of representatives of data for the issuing of a report by the Commission of Enquiry into the system at present obtaining with regard to share transactions in Hongkong has been completed, the “China Mail” understands.

label: text

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: DISARMED TROOPS SENT TO CANTON.

label: text
text: BOAT TO BE RESTORED.

label: text
text: The disposal of the locally-owned steamer "Sui Yik" and also of the Cantonese troops and arms found on board the vessel, which has been, moored in the Admiralty anchorage since her capture in British waters last Saturday, has now been decided by the authorities.

label: text
text: The 150. disarmed Chinese soldiers were taken off the boat and conveyed to the Kowloon Railway station, where they entrained for Shumchun at noon to-day. They will be escorted until they are over the British border.

label: text
text: Prior to handing over the vessel to her local owners, the Fuk Hoi Company, a further search of the holds will be made. The vessel will be taken alongside the Police Pier at Kowloon for this purpose.

label: text
text: The arms and ammunition found on the vessel will be confiscated.

Holyoak at the Legislative Council meeting to-day, the Colonial Secretary stated that if no unforeseen circumstances arise, it is hoped to complete and open Saiyingpun School by the 30th June, 1926. The work was delayed for about two months mainly owing to the Strike.

label: paragraph_title
text: SWATOW IMPROVES.

label: text
text: CARGO LANDED BY S.S. "HYDRANGEA."

label: text
text: BOX COTT BELIEVED OVER.

label: text
text: This morning the s.s. "Hydrangea" returned to Hongkong from Swatow.

label: text
text: There was no incident in the voyage. All the cargo shipped from Hongkong was landed and fresh cargo was brought back. About a hundred passengers also travelled from Swatow on the ship.

label: text
text: The agritators are now believed to have put a good distance between themselves and the port of Swatow and the anti-foreign boycott has been described as all over.

label: paragraph_title
text: DOLLAR INTERESTS.

label: text
text:
MORE SHIPPING BOARD
BUDS?

label: text
text: MONOPOL a ESTION.

label: text
text: So steamship company was interested at the time in these eve boats, negotiations centring entirely around the Pacific Mail boats, but there have been rumours for some time of negotiations proceeding. Between the Dollar interests and the Shipping Board for the forecast of these vessels also, Reports from Seattle that such negotiations are proceeding were confirmed by Rear Admiral Palmer, president of the Emergency Ship Corporation, in charge of ship entes.

label: text
text: Enquiries at the Hongkong office elicited no information of a definite nature, the only thing that was known being that the Board were seeking for purchasers of the vessels. There would be little change even if the Admiral Oriental Line purchased the ships, the "China Mail" was informed. They were already operated by this line on commission and the difference would be entirely a domestic one.

label: text
text:
The bouts concerned are the President. "Madison," "Jackson," "McKinley," "Jefferson," and "Grant" and there are also freighters but whether they form the subject of negotiations is not known. If the five boats mentioned are taken over by the Dollar interests they will be the operators of practically ex-American vessel in the Oriental trade; only two other lines operating Shipping Board ships being in the Pacific.
The question of advisability of such a monopoly has been raised in America but Shipping Board officials belittle its significance and refer to the competition with Japanese and Canadian ships on the Orient run which would make impossible any freight or passenger rate inflation.

label: text
text: In this connection it is interesting to recall that when interviewed on the subject of possible monopoly whilst on a visit to Hongkong, Capt. Robert Dollar said that the prosperity of his Company was so mextricably bound up with that of the various countries about the Pacific Ocean that fears regarding a monopoly had no possible foundation in fact.

text: A Chinese woman passenger on a motor truck travelling from Un Long to Mongkok was fatally injured in Taipo Road yesterday afternoon.

As the vehicles passed a crash was heard and on investigation he found one of his passengers with a wound in the head caused by a projecting beam. The injured woman was taken to the Kwong Wah Hospital but died on the way. The timber-laden jerry got away without stopping after the accident but it was forced as No. 1400 Tom driver as including names.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title

CANTON STUDENTS
FINED

label: text
text: SEDITIONS LITERATURE CHAPGE.

label: text
text: Possession of a seditious pamphlet and two Chinese newspapers containing pernicious references to the boycott position led to two Chinese students being brought before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Central Magistracy yesterday. The students came from Swatow by the s.s. "Haining" and the documents were found in their luggage when searched on the wharf.

label: text
text: One of the accused was fined $25, and the other was remanded until this morning as he wished to call a witness.

label: text
text: A shopkeeper from Shamshuipo informed His Worship that he was acquainted with the accused, who was a student from the Kwangtung University, and he had never heard of the man getting into trouble during the time he was in Hongkong.

label: text
text: His Worship was satisfied that the accused had no intention of passing the documents round and imposed a fine of $25.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: FENNY'S GREAT CHINESE FENTIVAL

label: text
text: ENIERRES CONCUBINE.

label: text
text: Moin-eoke festival, or, Mid-Autumn Festival, or Chung-chin which to give its chiscal rendering, falls this year on Friday (to tomorrow the 15th day of the 8th moon.

label: text
text: Tradition places its origin about 2,150 B.C., when Wiedith famous which emperor Hao I (Hao Ngai in Cantonese). He shot nine of the ten suns illuminating the heavens when the sun-goet besought him not to make a butt's eye of the tenth. For this been he was given a motion which would make him immortal with a home in the sun. Before he could take the potion which had to be prepared in an turn at night with devout prayers meanwhile, a naughty concubine by name of Sheung Ngo-drinad, the last drop while her spouse slept through, the wake night service. Light as a fairy the woman fled to the moon to escape the archer's wrath. Every year she returns to mother earth and moon-cakes are eaten in her honour.

label: text
text: This episode has been commercialised into a favourite stage-play being one of the star numbers of Mei Lan-fung's repertoire. Mei will be remembered as the famous Northern actor who was down here in 1922. The legend has been slightly lengthened and ends up with Hao I being thrown out of the moon after a hot pursuit of his concubine.

label: text
text:
It is a harvest festival in that the tea-houses reap their annual harvest. Moon-shaped cakes with wonderful ingredients are made months ahead of the festival and shipped to all parts of the world where Chinese are to be found. Chinese delight in the delicacies. All other aspect is the making and sale of beautiful lanterns with which Chimatown will be decorated with a night.
Actually the men-folk take little note of the religious side of the festival except to organise a feast at West Point. Schools and various working guilds make a holiday of it and it is also one of the four settlement days in Chinese business circles. The women, of course, must "chin-chin joss."

label: text
text:
This business settlement, of course, will not be like that of other years, owing to financial stringency. With the announcement of the £3,000,000 loan, there is practically no possibility of a panic.
A special week of celebration is announced for the Lee Gardens, East Point.

label: text
text: CANTON AND THE "WAH SHAN."

label: text
text: Having secured control of the s.s. "Wah Shan," which was recently captured whilst on her way from Kwong-chow-wan with foodstuffs for Hongkong, the Canton authorities are converting her into a naval transport vessel. It will be recalled that some time after the vessel was taken to Canton, the authorities ordered that she be handed over to the Government, the pretext given being that she had military officers on board when she was seized, and that, moreover, political documents were found on the ship. The decision to transfer the steamer to the Canton Navy was taken at a meeting of the Central Executive Committee of the Government recently held, at which it was pointed out that the vessel was strongly built of steel and was capable of doing a good speed, thus making her a valuable addition to the naval transport fleet. The "Wah Shan" is a small coasting steamer of about 300 tons, and was employed on the run between Hongkong, Macao and Kwang-chow-wan. Her utterly illegal seizure whilst engaged in the transport of merchandise to Hongkong, says "Shipping and Engineering," constituted an set of hostility to Hongkong, in that it was part and parcel of the Canton scheme to cut off food supplies from the Colony, and the taking over of the vessel by the Canton Government for incorporation in the so-called Navy in our country equally irregular.
